items.name: Alma Hightower
items.who_is_this: Minnie Hightower's mother; the teacher who led the Melodic Dots youth group Liston played in as a girl in Los Angeles
items.summary: Liston played in Miss Hightower's Melodic Dots, toured to a fair in the back of a truck, learned stagecraft from her, and stayed with her until she joined the union at 16.
items.one_liner: her first bandleader and stage teacher
items.her_quote: She was nice to me. I stayed with her until 16 and I joined the union and started to work at the Lincoln Theater. I think she was kind of pissed off with me then.
items.bryant_quote: Miss Hightower seemed to have had quite an attachment. She thought you were just the greatest.
items.notes: Not truly absent but folded: her_relationships.json puts 'Miss Hightower' and 'Mrs. Hightower' as surface forms of Minnie Hightower (Liston's schoolmate). The transcript distinguishes them: Bryant says Minnie 'told you about Mrs. Hightower' (295546), and the transcriber identifies 'Minnie Hightower, her mother Miss Hightower' (296332). The first name Alma is not in the transcript; it is supplied from outside knowledge for spelling only and should be checked. Other good Liston lines: 'Everything that was on the stage, she taught us' (295559); 'Miss Hightower and the Melodic Dots.' (295555).

items.name: Doddard Deal
items.who_is_this: her music teacher at junior high school in Los Angeles (McKinley Junior High), who wanted to adopt her so he could send her away to study
items.summary: Liston said her junior-high music teacher was a good all-round teacher who wanted to adopt her to send her places, and she refused because she wanted to stay with her mother.
items.one_liner: junior-high music teacher who wanted to adopt her
items.her_quote: He was good. He didn’t mess with me. He just was a good teacher for all around.
items.bryant_quote: But he wanted to adopt you?
items.notes: The name exists only in the transcriber's bracket and is marked uncertain ('?Doddard Deal'); Liston says only 'Mr.' before it. Treat the spelling as unverified. Second Liston line: 'he would have to adopt me to send me to all of these places... I told him, “No. I want to stay with my mom.”' (295533).

items.name: Quincy Jones
items.who_is_this: the musician Liston called in to conduct her arrangements at a Gloria Lynne recording date (dated 1959 by Bryant) when she was ill
items.summary: Liston said that when she was sick on the day of the Gloria Lynne session she called Quincy Jones, who conducted for her, though almost all the arrangements were hers.
items.one_liner: conducted her arrangements when she was ill
items.her_quote: Yeah, and I was sick, and the day of the recording date, I was out of it, so I called Quincy
items.notes: Surname is the transcriber's bracketed expansion; the quote stops before it. The block continues: 'he conducted for me, but all of the arrangements are mine – almost all of them.' No tie term fits a conductor standing in for her; 'unknown' used.

items.name: Abbey Lincoln
items.who_is_this: a singer Liston wrote arrangements for
items.summary: Asked about Abbey Lincoln, Liston said she was fine and that she still wrote for her now and then.
items.her_quote: Oh, she’s fine. I write for her now and then.
items.notes: Bryant's question is just 'What about Abbey Lincoln?' (295883).

items.name: Ben
items.who_is_this: her mother's husband; the tune Ben Loves Lu was dedicated to him and her mother
items.summary: Liston closed the interview with Ben Loves Lu, a tune she dedicated to her mother and her mother's husband, and said it might become her theme song.
items.one_liner: her mother's husband, honoured in a tune
items.her_quote: And we’ll close with a tune dedicated to my mom and her man, her husband, Ben Loves Lu.
items.notes: her_relationships.json has an item named 'Ben Loves Lu' (relation 'friend of', proposed 'her husband'), i.e. the tune title was taken as the person; the person Ben has no proper entry. The transcript does not say whether he is the 'pop' whose favourite was Cab Calloway (295499); do not merge without evidence. 'Lu' presumably refers to her mother (Lucille, named only in a bracket) but the transcript does not say so. Liston's two husbands are a separate matter (Nelson Harris is already listed).

items.name: Clifford Burden
items.who_is_this: Minnie Hightower's husband; father of Clifford, Jr.; appears in an old photograph with the Melodic Dots circle
items.summary: Asked whether she knew Clifford Burden, Liston said yes and asked whether he and Minnie were both dead.
items.one_liner: minnie hightower's husband, known to her
items.her_quote: Oh yeah. He and Minnie both dead, huh?
items.notes: her_relationships.json has 'Clifford, Jr.' (the son) with surface forms ['Clifford', 'Clifford, Jr.']; the father is a different person and has no entry. Bryant: 'that’s who Minnie married' (296335). The bracket in 296337 names a 'Clifford' in a photograph — which Clifford is not stated.

items.name: Valaida Snow
items.who_is_this: a performer Bryant asked about in connection with the Lincoln Theater years
items.summary: Bryant asked about Valaida Snow, and Liston could not recall details beyond saying everybody came through the Lincoln Theater in her time there.
items.one_liner: asked about; liston could not recall
items.notes: Name appears only inside the transcriber's bracketed summary of Bryant's question. Liston's reply: '[cannot recall details.] I had a year or a year and a half there, so everybody came through there.' — not a statement about Snow.

items.name: Charlie Parker
items.who_is_this: saxophonist Bryant cites as a starting point young players reach back to
items.summary: Bryant said David Sanchez reached back to musicians 'from Bird on up'; Liston said nothing about Parker.
items.bryant_quote: He reached back to a lot of guys from Bird on up.
items.notes: 'Bird' identified as Charlie Parker by recognition of the nickname. Not to be confused with Birdland (a club), which Liston mentions.

items.name: Jimmy Rowles
items.summary: Bryant identified Stacey Rowles as 'Jimmie's daughter' while listing young women players.
items.one_liner: named by bryant only, as a father
items.bryant_quote: Trumpet players: Stacey Rowles. Jimmie’s daughter.
items.notes: Surname inferred from 'Stacey Rowles. Jimmie’s daughter.'; the transcript gives only 'Jimmie'. The pipeline's 'Jimmie' surface form belongs to Jimmie Lunceford, a different person.

items.name: Roz
items.who_is_this: the woman whose band was later taken over by the reed player Bryant describes (the Ann Patterson / Maiden Voyage passage)
items.summary: Bryant mentioned that a Los Angeles women's band had been Roz's before another reed player took it over.
items.notes: Surname exists only as the transcriber's uncertain bracket '[?Crans]'; possibly Roz Cron, but that is outside recognition and unverified. Liston says nothing about her.
